Building Wire: Indoor electrical conductors used to wire branch circuits, outlets, switches, and lighting within residential and commercial buildings.
Commercial HVAC: Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems used in large commercial buildings, including chillers, rooftop units, heat exchangers, and associated motor coils.
Commercial Trunk Lines: Large-gauge feeder conductors that carry power from a commercial service entrance or main panel to downstream sub-panels and distribution points throughout a building.
Distribution Lines: Medium-voltage utility conductors that carry electricity from substations to end-use customers across neighborhoods and commercial districts.
Drip Loop Cable: Overhead service-entrance conductors formed into a downward curve at the weatherhead to shed rainwater before the wire enters the meter base or service panel.
EV Busbar: Rigid high-current conductors that route power between major electrical components within a battery-electric vehicle's powertrain.
EV Interconnect: Conductive tabs or strips that electrically connect individual battery cells to one another within an electric vehicle battery pack.
EV Traction Motor Winding: Electromagnetic coils wound into the stator of an electric vehicle traction motor to generate the rotating magnetic field that drives the vehicle.
EV Wire Harness: Bundled power and signal wiring assemblies that interconnect electrical and electronic systems throughout a battery-electric vehicle.
ICE Alternator: An onboard generator driven by an internal combustion engine that produces alternating current to charge the vehicle battery and power electrical loads.
ICE Busbar: Rigid conductors that distribute electrical power among components within a conventional internal combustion engine vehicle's electrical system.
ICE Wire Harness: Bundled low-voltage wiring assemblies that connect electrical and electronic components throughout a conventional internal combustion engine vehicle.
Industrial Trunk Line: Heavy-gauge feeder conductors that supply high-ampacity power to industrial loads such as motors, drives, and process equipment within factories and plants.
Motors: General-purpose electric motors used in industrial and commercial applications, containing stator windings that convert electrical energy into mechanical rotation.
Residential HVAC: Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems used in homes, including split-system air conditioners, heat pumps, and their associated coils and fans.
Residential Trunk Lines: Main service-entrance and feeder conductors that carry power from the utility meter to the home's main distribution panel.
Solar Array: Outdoor direct-current cables that connect photovoltaic panels to each other and to inverters within a solar energy installation.
Solar PV Module: A photovoltaic panel assembly consisting of interconnected solar cells enclosed in a protective frame, which converts sunlight directly into direct-current electricity.
Transformer: A static electrical device that uses inductive windings to step voltage up or down between two circuits for power transmission or distribution.
Transmission Line: High-voltage conductors that carry bulk electrical power over long distances from generating stations to regional substations.
Wind Array Cables: Medium-voltage inter-array cables that connect individual wind turbines to each other and to a collector substation within a wind farm.
Wind Drip: Flexible power cables routed in a downward loop from a wind turbine's nacelle or tower junction box to prevent water ingress into the electrical enclosure.
